attempts.sql: WITH api AS (SELECT symbol_id FROM code.symbols WHERE file_id = 'auto_ontology/server/models.py' AND name = 'ApiModel' AND kind = 'class'), direct AS (SELECT DISTINCT cb.class_symbol_id FROM code.class_bases cb JOIN api ON cb.base_symbol_id = api.symbol_id) SELECT ca.class_symbol_id, MIN(ca.depth) AS depth FROM code.class_ancestry ca JOIN api ON ca.ancestor_symbol_id = api.symbol_id WHERE ca.depth >= 2 AND ca.class_symbol_id NOT IN (SELECT class_symbol_id FROM direct) GROUP BY ca.class_symbol_id ORDER BY depth, class_symbol_id

request:
Which classes inherit from ApiModel (auto_ontology/server/models.py) only indirectly, i.e. through at least one intermediate class of this repository, and do not name ApiModel directly in their class statement? An import alias of ApiModel (auto_ontology/server/responses.py imports it as _Payload) counts as naming ApiModel directly, and a subscripted base such as ListResponse[T] counts as its class. For each, give the class symbol ID and the length of the shortest inheritance chain to ApiModel (2 when the parent class directly subclasses ApiModel).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), depth (integer).
explanation: Finds the ApiModel class in auto_ontology/server/models.py, then uses transitive class ancestry to find classes reaching it at depth >= 2. It excludes classes that name ApiModel (or an alias resolving to it) directly as a base, and reports the shortest inheritance depth for each remaining class.
sql: WITH api AS (SELECT symbol_id FROM code.symbols WHERE file_id = 'auto_ontology/server/models.py' AND name = 'ApiModel' AND kind = 'class'), direct AS (SELECT DISTINCT cb.class_symbol_id FROM code.class_bases cb JOIN api ON cb.base_symbol_id = api.symbol_id) SELECT ca.class_symbol_id, MIN(ca.depth) AS depth FROM code.class_ancestry ca JOIN api ON ca.ancestor_symbol_id = api.symbol_id WHERE ca.depth >= 2 AND ca.class_symbol_id NOT IN (SELECT class_symbol_id FROM direct) GROUP BY ca.class_symbol_id ORDER BY depth, class_symbol_id
